title: First seeing Louis Armstrong at the Howard Theater
summary: He saw Armstrong in Washington about 1930, once giving him a knife for a corn; Armstrong later said he overblew then.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I remember when I first saw Louis when he came through Washington, this was about 1930, somewhere around that time. I'd heard him a lot on records, but when I first got to really see him good was in Washington. He came there. He had -- at the Howard Theater -- he had -- he used to cut his hair in a pompadour. He would cut all out of the back of his hair, and this thing would be up front, and he would slick that back, you know.

I remember when I was a kid around there, I gave Louis -- his corn was hurting him -- I gave him a little knife to pick his corn. But he never did forget that. It was around 1930. And you look at time now, that's almost 50 years ago. When I think of it, that's a long time ago.

But he was playing and, oh, boy, he was playing. He told me that in later years, he said, he didn't know how to preserve himself then, and he almost blew his lip out, you know, he had a lot of cuts on his lip, because he blew -- overblew, and he was strong and young, and he blew too hard, you know.
